sections.name: Boo
sections.card:
Summary: A ghost found on every board that steals coins or a Star from another player on behalf of whoever uses it, and the Boo Bell item calls one up on demand. The wiki's Boo page says Boos behave in Mario Party 3 exactly as in the previous two games.
Weak points: If a Boo goes after your coins you can fight it off by pressing the A button quickly (the Mario Party 2 rule, which the Boo page says Boos still follow in Mario Party 3). Holding a Boo Repellant makes the Boo flee without stealing anything.
Looks like: Usually a white round ghost with stubby arms and a small tail, with a wide smile showing four upper fangs and a large tongue.
Tips: Under the Mario Party 2 rules, which the Boo page says carry over, Boo charges five coins to steal coins and can take at most 30 coins or one Star. On Waluigi's Island a Boo instead offers you two paths, one of them rigged to send you back to the start. Boo is also a Duel Mode partner: Yoshi starts with one, and it counterattacks for equal damage.

sections.name: Bowser and the Bowser Space
sections.card:
Summary: Landing on a Bowser Space makes Bowser appear, and he usually tries to steal coins, may give you items, or may curse every player. Bowser Spaces are fairly rare, one to five per board by default.
Weak points: In Mario Party 3 the event roulette is not random: it always stops on the event the cursor is hanging over when you press the button, so with precise timing you pick the event. A player with no coins is spared: Bowser pays 30, 40 or 50 coins depending on placement and no event happens, and no Stars are lost.
Looks like: Bowser flashes a color when an event starts: purple for Bowser's Curse, green for Bowser's Reverse Curse, yellow for Bowser Shuffle and red for Bowser Revolution.
Tips: Bowser's Curse limits every player's next move to 1 to 3 spaces, like a Poison Mushroom, and Bowser's Reverse Curse makes every player move backwards on their next turn, like a Reverse Mushroom, unless they use an item that cancels the effect. Bowser Shuffle randomly shuffles all four players' positions, and he can also hand you a Bowser Phone (rarely two) or a Bowser Suit for free.

sections.name: Game Guy and the Game Guy Space
sections.card:
Summary: A game-show host who takes all your coins when you land on his space, then runs a luck-based minigame in which you either get them back doubled (or more) or lose them all. Game Guy Spaces turn up in both Party Mode and Duel Mode.
Weak points: His four minigames are Game Guy's Lucky 7, Game Guy's Magic Boxes, Game Guy's Roulette and Game Guy's Sweet Surprise, and they are mostly luck-based. Players can usually double their coins or lose all of them, though they can risk their money for higher multiples.
Looks like: A Shy Guy with a yellowish mask and a bowtie.
Tips: The Lucky Charm item sends a chosen player, even yourself, to a Game Guy minigame without landing on his space. You can practice in Game Guy's Room: you start with 10 coins, can bet up to 100, and aim for 1,000; winning unlocks the rare minigame Mario's Puzzle Party Pro, but the room itself opens only after Story Mode is beaten with at least eight S rankings.

sections.name: Evil Woody
sections.card:
Summary: The sour tree on the Woody Woods board: land on one of the Happening Spaces around him and he makes you pick a fruit that costs you, either a Minus Coin Fruit (lose five coins) or a Reverse Block Fruit (roll and move backwards).
Weak points: You choose one of the two fruits yourself, but if you pick neither Evil Woody always gives you the Reverse Block Fruit, so the only way to avoid the backwards move is to choose the Minus Coin Fruit.
Looks like: The mirror image of Woody: blue with purple leaves and a permanently angry expression.
Tips: Three ? Spaces surround Evil Woody. The kind Woody on the same board offers a Plus Coin Fruit (five coins) or a Plus Block Fruit (a second dice roll) instead, and if you pick neither he gives you the extra Dice Block.

sections.name: Deep Bloober Sea's torpedo and anglerfish traps
sections.card:
Summary: Deep Bloober Sea's sea creatures work against you: a Sushi in a submarine can blast you onto the other path, a giant vacuum anglerfish can suck you in and spit you out, and a giant Blooper Baby calls its mother to carry you across the board.
Weak points: At the submarine junction three of the four buttons do nothing and one fires a torpedo that blasts you to the opposite path; the buttons do not reset until the incorrect one is chosen, and sometimes the Sushi fails to notice you at all. Against the anglerfish, keep tapping the button to swim against the suction, or you are sucked in.
Looks like: A Sushi (a shark) in a submarine looking over the main junction, a giant vacuum anglerfish with an arrow on it that spins, and a giant Blooper Baby.
Tips: The anglerfish's arrow stops pointing to the bottom, the front or the right, and a player who is sucked in lands near a Sushi, near Boo, or back at the start. Of the board's 93 spaces, 5 are Bowser Spaces and 2 are Game Guy Spaces.

sections.name: Waluigi's Island's dynamite and rigged path
sections.card:
Summary: An unlockable board full of traps: each time someone lands on a Happening Space on the dynamite island a number counts down from 5, and when it reaches 0 the dynamite explodes and anyone caught in the blast loses all their coins.
Weak points: To get off the dynamite island you jump onto the gear in the center during the Action Time: the arrow that is flashing when you land is the path you must take, and if it stops on the down arrow, or you take too long, you stay on the island. On the way to Boo there are two paths and one is booby-trapped, which sends you back to the start.
Looks like: A circle of dynamite with a number in the middle of the explosives, set at five at the start, and a gear in the center of the board with four flashing arrows.
Tips: The Happening Spaces are the dangerous ones on the dynamite island. On the island in the upper left every space changes to another type each turn, except the Bank Space, and the red pipes along the top sides all lead to the green pipe near the start.

sections.name: Chain Chomp (duel partner)
sections.card:
Summary: A chainless Chain Chomp that can be a Duel Mode partner; its attack hits the opponent and all their partners at once. Its attack is 1, its stamina 2 and its salary six coins.
Weak points: Its attack is 1. A Boo partner hits back at a Chain Chomp's multi-attack only if the Boo is directly in front of the attacking Chain Chomp.
Looks like: Series pages describe a Chain Chomp as a black or dark blue ball with big round eyes and a large gaping mouth of sharp teeth; the Duel Mode partner has no chain.
Tips: No character starts with a Chain Chomp; it comes from the partner lottery. When it is powered up it grows to the size of a Shark Chomp, jumps up and body slams all opponents. A Bob-omb and a Chomp together earn a "dangerous duo" comment from the Millennium Star, but no attack boost.

sections.name: Thwomp (duel partner)
sections.card:
Summary: A Duel Mode partner with 0 attack that crushes the opponent's partners instantly but does nothing to the opposing player. Its stamina is 2 and its salary four coins.
Weak points: It never hurts your hearts, only your partners. A Boo partner that a Thwomp defeats does not hit back as it normally would.
Looks like: Series pages describe Thwomps as living stone blocks, usually rectangular and spiked, often with an angry face.
Tips: No character starts with a Thwomp, so one only arrives through the partner roulette. With two Thwomps the Millennium Star lowers their salaries by one instead of raising their attack, and the Millennium Star calls a Whomp and a Thwomp an earth shaking combination. The instruction booklet wrongly gives it an attack of 2.

sections.name: Boo Repellant
sections.card:
Summary: A spray can that makes Boo flee without stealing from you. Toad sells it for 10 coins, and the manual spells it Boo Repellent.
Uses: It activates by itself when Boo tries to steal coins or a Star from you while you hold it, and Boo leaves with nothing. Each can is good for one use.
Tips: You can throw one away at the start of your turn to make room in your inventory, which counts as using an item that turn. Other players tend to avoid wasting a Boo attempt on you, but computer players do not care and will try anyway, even for Stars.

sections.name: Boo Bell
sections.card:
Summary: Rings up Boo to steal coins or a Star from an opponent. Baby Bowser sells it for 15 coins.
Uses: Using it summons Boo, who asks whom you want him to steal from and what to steal. The manual says he steals coins or a Star from another player.
Tips: A player holding a Boo Repellant drives Boo off without losing anything. The Boo Bell is sold in Baby Bowser's shop, the one that sells items meant to hinder opponents.

sections.name: Plunder Chest
sections.card:
Summary: A treasure chest that steals an item from an opponent you choose. Baby Bowser's shop sells it for 10 coins, and it is Princess Peach's favorite item.
Uses: You pick which opponent to rob, and the item taken is chosen randomly if that player holds more than one. The stolen item cannot be used before you roll.
Tips: The Barter Box works in a similar way, but the Plunder Chest only steals one item while the Barter Box swaps all of them. Computer-controlled Peach prioritizes it when she can get it.

sections.name: Lucky Lamp
sections.card:
Summary: A lamp that holds Mushroom Jeanie, who moves the Star to a different space. Baby Bowser's shop sells it for 10 coins, and it is the counterpart of the Magic Lamp.
Uses: When used, Mushroom Jeanie appears at the Star space and moves the Star to a different location on the board, instead of taking you to it as the Magic Lamp does. The manual says she moves the Millennium Star to a new location on your command.
Tips: In Spiny Desert, where one Millennium Star is a mirage, she always goes to the real one. Besides Baby Bowser's shop, the Lucky Lamp can be won in an item minigame.

sections.name: Bowser Phone
sections.card:
Summary: Calls Bowser to give one player a Bowser event, as if they had landed on a Bowser Space. Baby Bowser's shop sells it for 10 coins.
Uses: You choose one of your opponents, or yourself, for Bowser to run one of his events on, and you can view the board before deciding. Choosing "Who do you think?" lets Bowser pick a random player.
Tips: The chosen player actually goes to meet Bowser at the same castle location as the Bowser Space. A Bowser Space can also hand you a Bowser Phone for free.

sections.name: Lucky Charm
sections.card:
Summary: A rare coin with Game Guy's face on one side that forces a chosen player to risk all their coins in a Game Guy minigame. No shop sells it.
Uses: Using it summons Game Guy, who takes all of the target's coins and starts a Game Guy minigame. The target can be another player or yourself, and the booklet says it lets you send another player to the Game Guy Room to risk all their coins.
Tips: You can get one from an Item Space by meeting Toad, rarely from a Hidden Block, or from an Item Bag bought at Baby Bowser's Joint.

sections.name: Wacky Watch
sections.card:
Summary: A rare item that jumps the game to exactly five turns before the end. It cannot be bought in any Item Shop.
Uses: Using it sets the turn number to exactly five turns before the game ends, so it can drastically shorten the game, or make it longer when used within five turns of the end.
Tips: You can get one by meeting Toad on an Item Space or finding it in a Hidden Block, and it is the only item in Mario Party 3 that neither an Item Shop nor an Item Bag gives you. If you use it on what would otherwise be the final turn, the rest of that turn is still played as the final turn, so the Item Shops stay closed.
